I am planning to work on a dark version soon. How should both themes contrast with each other?

Typogra Dark has been planned since the inception of Typogra 2. When first rewriting and updating Typogra, I made a decision to make the light version the default, based off of the guess that it covered the most users. As you know, ever since Voat was redesigned, we introduced a new night mode, which created an issue with subverse CSS. I suggested a solution that enables two separate stylesheets to accommodate both day and night mode users and is planned for the future. Until the feature is implemented, styled subs must choose which version to style for.

I postponed Dark until support was added, but I recently started growing a little uncertain for the future. I don't know how much time I'll have in the future or what may happen, so I've decided to start working on Dark right away. But because that support isn't here yet, I will make it available as an alternative for now to give Typogra users a new option.

For now, I am still divided on how much of a contrast both themes should have. As Typogra currently is, it fits better with lighter backgrounds. I could either just overhaul the colors to match night mode or redesign it as its own night mode with a similar but different style altogether. What do you think?

I am absolutely up for a dark Typogra theme for users with night mode enabled - keep the same feel, just make it (essentially) a palette swap to the sole end of decreasing monitor light emissions.

Some things I'd suggest:

  • Use the dark texture as the bulk background instead of the current creamy-looking texture
  • Use a dark grey (one slightly lighter than the dark texture) for the little side widget things on the right.
  • For the header (the part with "VOAT | TYPOGRA | HOT|NEW|…"), make that slightly darker than it is right now.
  • The top-verses list at the top, leave alone. Its current color contrasts well with that odd header-background image.
  • Perhaps consider a slightly lighter replacement for the header-background image for the light theme.
  • The part on the right, with the very light background that says "Share a link | Start a discussion", make that a medium-light grey pattern.

I think if those changes are implemented, that will be 85% of what needs to happen, and at that point it'll just be minor tweaks left to make it pop.

You are awesome for taking the time to write that out.

You've made some good points that I'll consider when making the dark alternative. About the header background image: it was a public domain picture of a rose that I've filtered to fit the theme here. I have almost zero experience in actual images, so it took a long time to pick that one out. I'm not sure I'd be able to find a better one for the light version. :-)
How long does it take you to make such a theme from scratch?
Rougly speaking, I'd say about 28-33 hours total, from nothing to a full release.

First off, you'll need to sign up with CPA Grip Here: http://cpagrip.com/

The Method:

So it is a little like Yahoo answers with a twist. Now you can go to twitter and find some targeted traffic from peoples tweets. Twitter has an excellent search feature where as you can search anyones’s tweets for a particular niche or topic. In this case we are going to find a problem that a lot of people are having the same issues with. Basically, we are going to tell others on the world of twitter that we have a quick solution to their problem and offer a quick way to fix it. So let’s pick a problem to solve… This is an older niche but it has made me a lot of money using this method. The “YOLD” or Yellow Light of Death on the Playstation 3. Ok so now that I have the problem to solve let’s make some money with it.

Step 1. Found a problem that a lot of other twitter users are having

Completed that with the “YLOD”

Step 2. Find something that might fix the problem

All I did was google “fixing PS3” and found a guide on how to fix a playstation 3 in a PDF format. I downloaded the guide and made a RAR file out of it. Changed the name of the file to “FIX the YLOD on the PS3” and password protected the RAR file…

Step 3. Upload the password.txt to your PPD or CPA network

I just upload the password to the rar file to the PPD network and of course they need to complete the survey to get the password. But you probably all ready know this.. Just putting in the step..

Step 4. Find that Targeted Traffic.

So with you have come up with the relative problem niche to offer your solution you need to get the word out to other twitter users that you have the BEST solution to their problem.. Do a search on twitter for your niche keyword (or problem to solve) in my example I am going to use “YLOD PS3” When you do your search be sure to add “-http” to the end of your search. This step is basically a filter. It works just like a google search whereas you are going to subtract and filter out other marketers tweets but removing those tweets that have a link in them.. Now when you find relative tweets to the niche-problem you are going to reply to them. In your reply make sure you state the problem, how to fix it and mention that you have had the same problem. Keep it from sounding spammy. And put a link to your solution in the reply. Always you a url shortener when putting the link in, such as http://bit.ly or similar. NEVER post a direct link to the “solution” as it may get flagged and remember with twitter you only have so many characters to work with. And example of a tweet and reply would be:

http://i.imgur.com/1YNRc9M.png

So when I found the above tweet I clicked reply and wrote this.. “Sorry to hear about your PS3 man. I used this fix when it happened to me! http://bit.ly..........” Dollar signs all the way. Other possible problems to solve and some of these are my personal favorites.. 1. Picking up girls 2. Getting your girlfriend back 3. Making money - This always works……. 4. Game hacks and cheats 5. Losing weight 6. Boyfriend cheating 7. Cheating on Tests 8. Movie or TV show spoilers

So basically, in a nutshell we have identified a problem, found a solution (sort of) and offered that solution to others with the problem. Now the real secret to my success using this method is putting this on autopilot. I have not the time to do the searches and post the replies for this method to work effectively, so I outsource the tweets/replies to others. I usually pay between $0.02-$0.03 per tweet and generally get a converstion of about 20% on all those tweets. Generally speaking you can hire others to do most of the hard work since it is just copy/paste. I try to keep one niche per person hired to keep organized. This lets me keep track of what niche/problem is performing well or not and so that the person I hired does not send the wrong tweets/replies pertaining to the niche/problem. For about every $1.00 I spend outsourcing the tweets/replies I generally make about $10.00 . Simple math tells me that is about a 90% return on my investments. Pretty good I do say. Of course I generally do the research and find the solution and upload that solution before I outsource the tweets/replies but that only takes me about 15-30 minutes per niche. I then just give the person I hire a search term to put into the twitter search and the copy of the tweet/reply that they can copy and paste. At any given time I usually have over 100 niches where I am having replies sent to them with solutions. Depending on the niche/solution and how hot it is at the time. I have earned upwards of $500 per day using this method while spending less than $25 for the tweets/replies to be done.
